capabilities.name: Android WebView runtime security policy
capabilities.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:4 (INTERNET only), :5 (allowBackup=false, usesCleartextTraffic=false), :6 (exported launcher, no intent data read); MainActivity.java:178-187 (JS and DOM storage on; file/content access off; MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW; SafeBrowsing on; no JS window opening or multiple windows; third-party cookies off); :205-208 (SSL error leads to cancel); :151-153 (external browser only for https); no addJavascriptInterface anywhere; :219 loads <origin>/?companion=1. Weakness: :192-201 lets any non-gesture HTTPS navigation to any origin stay inside the WebView ('HTTPS redirects may be the trusted tunnel's sign-in flow').
capabilities.detail: TLS, cleartext, bridge and file-access controls are sound. Navigation is not restricted to the configured origin, there is no certificate pinning (system CA trust), and showConnection() (:103-150) never clears cookies or storage when the origin changes. None of this has been exercised on a device.

gaps.title: MA3 T5–T8 'production SQLite' observations read the development database, not production
gaps.detail: t8/audit.mjs:18-19 opens C:/Users/allam/AppData/Local/Bunny-A/development/host.sqlite. The same path is used in t7/production-audit.mjs:4, t6/final-audit.mjs:12 and t5/observe-production.mjs:3. state-paths.server.ts:9-11 defines that as the development directory, which belongs to the source dev Host on 43139 (MA3_BASELINE.md, process census). The installed production state root is ...\Bunny-A\state (test-results/ma3/production-restart/RESTART_RECORD.md:36; MA3_BASELINE.md §5). Result: T8 production-before.json:21-24 reports devices 0, tasks 0, projects 0, and T7 reports 'zero Project rows' (MA3_T7_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_ACCEPTANCE.md:114), while the production census reads 18 devices (1 active), 62 tasks and 13 projects (MA3_BASELINE.md:99-101). Scenario: T9 copies audit.mjs, pairs or revokes a device on production by mistake, and reports 'devices unchanged' from the dev DB.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Reuse the MA3 baseline census method instead (postboot-census-READONLY-script.mjs:4-10): copy state/host.sqlite, -wal and -shm into a temp directory and open the copy readOnly. Only do this if the T9 brief authorizes reading production. Otherwise label the production DB comparison NOT TESTED and correct the T5–T8 wording in the T9 report. Never point an audit at developmentStateDirectory().

gaps.title: No test exercises a paired device supervising Agents: Pause, Resume, Stop, or approving/denying/revoking a Host offer
gaps.detail: A device token reaches agentCommand with actor device:<id> for every AGENT_ACTION (http.server.ts:397-411). pause, resume and stop (agent-runtime.server.ts:900-905) and authorization approve/deny/revoke (:866-874, :888-899) have no device check, by design. No *.test.ts calls these with a device token or 'device:' actor (grep). Only refusals are tested: A33/A34 (agentic-authorization.test.ts:85-86) and HTTP adjust returning 400 (agentic-live.test.ts:89). Scenario: a phone POSTs {action:'agent.authorization.approve', data:{id, revision:<stale>}} or agent.resume on an Agent whose consent was revoked. Nothing proves the outcome over HTTP, nor that the event or provenance records 'paired-device' (agentic-store.server.ts:98).
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Add one disposable live test that reuses agentic-live.test.ts start(), /pair and device.token (lines 18-35, 86-91). As a device, run agent.list, agent.get, agent.pause, agent.resume (refused without consent, allowed with), agent.stop, approve of the exact current revision (allowed), approve of a stale revision (refused), extra keys (refused by http.server.ts:400-405) and deny/revoke. Assert canonical state and device provenance, then revoke the device and confirm 401 for each action.

gaps.title: A paired device can create new Agents (objective-only); untested and beyond the T9 supervise-only scope
gaps.detail: http.server.ts:398-399 refuses agent.create from a device only when data.steps is present. AgentRuntime.create (agent-runtime.server.ts:103-127) has no actor check and creates a Mission with origin 'agent:device:<id>'. Scenario: a phone sends commandBunnyHost {action:'agent.create', data:{objective:'...'}}. A new Host-planned Agent is created and occupies AGENT_LIMITS.maxActiveAgents slots (:109). The phone can then call agent.start or agent.authorization.approve on it (:856-857, :866-871). No test covers this.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: If T9 is supervise-only, refuse agent.create from non-local callers at the existing branch at http.server.ts:398 (extend the same CommandRefusedError) and add a device-token test. If remote creation is intended, test it explicitly and document it.

gaps.title: No per-device rights model; 'within device rights' means one fixed role
gaps.detail: The devices table holds only (id, name, token_hash, created_at, revoked_at): the insert at http.server.ts:343 and the schema in missions.test.ts:829. Remote authority is a single hardcoded non-local role (the `local` flag at http.server.ts:330-331, actor strings 'device:<id>'). Tokens have no expiry. The Host row never expires, and the cookie Max-Age is one year (bunny-pair.ts:16). Scenario: a lost phone keeps full remote-role authority until a workstation revoke.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Document in T9 that device rights are the single existing remote role, enforced at http.server.ts and agent-runtime.server.ts. Do not invent scopes. Make 'revoke a lost device' part of T9 acceptance, reusing device.revoke (:572-576).

gaps.title: Android WebView keeps arbitrary cross-origin HTTPS navigations in-app when there is no user gesture
gaps.detail: MainActivity.java:192-201 returns false (load in the WebView) for any https URL unless request.hasGesture() and the target is cross-origin. Scenario: a script- or redirect-initiated navigation, such as an artifact link that redirects or a tunnel error page, moves the WebView to https://attacker.example. That page then renders inside the 'Bunny-A' chrome with JS and DOM storage enabled (:179-180) and can phish a pairing code. The HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, origin-bound cookie is not exposed, so the risk is phishing, not token theft. There is also no certificate pinning (:205-208 relies on system trust).
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: In shouldOverrideUrlLoading, keep a navigation in the WebView only if ServerAddress.sameOrigin(serverUrl, destination). Open everything else with openBrowser(). Add the cases to android/tests/ServerAddressTest.java and rebuild with scripts/build-android.ps1.

gaps.title: Existing production 'Phone companion' credential is bound to a withdrawn quick-tunnel origin; physical phone control was never tested
gaps.detail: test-results/ma2-gate7/post-signin/device-preservation.json:3-9 records id a307ff4b-2d0b-425e-88b9-84eaf1302506, name 'Phone companion', createdAt 1791174129259 (2026-10-05T04:22:09Z), revokedAt null. That time falls inside the T6 invitation window: 04:15:39–04:25:39Z for origin martin-lovely-myself-tomatoes.trycloudflare.com (test-results/ma2-gate6/android-installation.json:10-12). That origin later returned 530/1033 and was withdrawn (MA2_T6_REMOTE_ACCEPTANCE.md:143-146). Cookies are per origin, so the phone must pair again at any new hostname (BUNNY_REMOTE.md:48). The name is the UI default (src/components/island/phone.tsx:219), so it does not prove APK vs browser. Device-side approval and Stop are NOT TESTED (MA2_T6:97-102, :285; MA3_T8:25). Scenario: T9 asks the user to 'use the existing Phone'. It fails at the new origin, re-pairing adds an 18th+ row, and the old active credential remains.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Plan T9 physical acceptance as a fresh pairing at the current origin, with the user present. Record model and Android version. Leave a307ff4b untouched unless the user explicitly asks to revoke it. Classify the phone rows NOT TESTED if the user does not take part.

gaps.title: Paired-device path through the T8 SSE bridge and live-update latency over a quick tunnel are unverified
gaps.detail: bunny-events.ts:33-45 forwards a device cookie token to Host /events. T8 stream-probe.mjs:6-23 tested only loopback workstation requests and denials (stream-live-probe.json). MA2_T6_REMOTE_ACCEPTANCE.md:85-88 says quick tunnels do not support SSE. The client falls back to invalidation every 30 s (host-stream.ts:54). Scenario: a phone over the quick tunnel sees a pending Agent approval up to 30 s late. Revocation mid-stream through the bridge (rather than direct Host /events) has no test.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Extend stream-probe.mjs, or add a test, using a disposable gateway with BUNNY_REMOTE_ORIGIN=https://<name>. Send Host: <name> and x-forwarded-proto: https over loopback (host-bridge.server.ts:30, :40) with a bunny_device cookie. Assert a signals-only stream, then revoke and assert closure. Document the polling bound for the phone.

gaps.title: authorizeBridge remote branch and pairing route lack unit tests
gaps.detail: host-bridge.server.test.ts:16-22 covers only 'not configured' and 'configured origin + cookie'. Untested: Origin mismatch (host-bridge.server.ts:33), sec-fetch-site cross-site (:32), an http remote origin (:40), a missing cookie (token null leads to 'Pair this device' at :58), the 401 to re-pair mapping (:62), and clientKey trusting spoofable cf-connecting-ip and x-forwarded-for (:46-48). bunny-pair.ts (local refusal :10, bounds :12, cookie flags :16) has no test.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Add cases to src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.test.ts, which already runs in the npm test lane via src/lib/orch/*.test.ts. Add a handler test for bunny-pair.ts against a disposable startHost.

gaps.title: Host-level remote refusals and pairing expiry have no tests; A33 test name overstates coverage
gaps.detail: No *.test.* file references 'Remote devices cannot supply executable Agent graphs' (http.server.ts:399), 'Remote approval can only answer the exact Host offer' (:405), 'Pairing can only be initiated on the workstation' (:560) or 'Device revocation requires workstation access' (:573). The 10-minute expiry (:562) is untested. agentic-authorization.test.ts:85 is named 'A33 revoked device authority...' but only passes the actor 'device:revoked' to agentCommand and never revokes anything.
gaps.suggestedMinimalFix: Add these as device-token HTTP assertions in the same disposable test as G2. Inject a clock, or wait for expiry against a short test hook only if one already exists. Otherwise label expiry STATIC VERIFIED.

gaps.title: T8 seal lacks a .gitattributes rule while core.autocrlf=true
gaps.detail: .gitattributes:8-13 marks the T5–T7 evidence and reports -text, with no rule for T8. `git config core.autocrlf` is true. verify-evidence.mjs:18 compares Git blob bytes to working-tree bytes, and INDEX.sha256 hashes LF bytes (seal-evidence.mjs:13-15). A fresh Windows checkout could produce CRLF and fail verification. Also, test-results/ is gitignored (.gitignore:8), so evidence must be force-added (T8 used a NUL pathspec file, seal-evidence.mjs:58-59).
